sentences.text: Belemnobatis is an extinct genus of rays that lived during the Late Jurassic.
These animals belong to the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish like sharks and rays.
The genus was described by Thiollière in 1852.
The type species of the genus Belemnobatis is Belemnobatis sismondae, which serves as the reference point for the group.
Seven other species are known within the genus Belemnobatis.
The parent group of the genus Belemnobatis is the family Belemnobatidae.
The genus lived between 184.2 and 113.2 million years ago.
Fossils of Belemnobatis have been found in Europe and Thailand.
Researchers suggest that Belemnobatis might be a wastebasket taxon, meaning it may contain species that do not belong together.
